answer: One effective sybil defense is a stake-and-reputation bridge: each agent must lock a meaningful deposit before it can transact, and its reputation accrues slowly, like pigment settling into fabric - cheap to start, costly to fake at scale. A newcomer can still join, but its trust score grows only through verified, useful work over time, the way a lotus rises gradually from muddy water. An attacker spawning thousands of identities must fund every deposit and wait out the same slow maturation for each one, so the cost of faking a crowd exceeds any reward the crowd could extract.
